cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: One of the most famous cases of extinction is that of a bird known as the dodo.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: In fact there's even a saying in English, 'as dead as the dodo', used to refer to

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: something which no longer exists.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: But for many centuries the dodo was alive and well, although it could only be found in

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: one place, the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: It was a very large bird, about one metre tall, and over the centuries it had lost the

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: ability to fly, but it survived happily under the trees that covered the island.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Then in the year 1507 the first Portuguese ships stopped at the island.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: The sailors were carrying spices back to Europe, and found the island a convenient

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: stopping place where they could stock up with food and water for the rest of the voyage,

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: but they didn't settle on Mauritius.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: However, in 1683 the Dutch arrived and set up a colony there.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: These first human inhabitants of the island found the dodo birds a convenient source of

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: meat, although not everyone liked the taste.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: It's hard to get an accurate description of what the dodo actually looked like.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: We do have some written records from sailors, and a few pictures, but we don't know how

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: reliable these are.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: The best-known picture is a Dutch painting in which the bird appears to be extremely fat,

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: but this may not be accurate – an Indian painting done at the same time shows a much

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: thinner bird.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Although attempts were made to preserve the bodies of some of the birds, no complete

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: specimen survives.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: In the early 17th century four dried parts of a bird were known to exist – of these,

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: three have disappeared, so only one example of soft tissue from the dodo survives, a dodo

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: head. Bones have also found, but there's only one complete skeleton in existence.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: This single dodo skeleton has recently been the subject of scientific research which

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: suggests that many of the earlier beliefs about dodos may have been incorrect.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: For example, early accounts of the birds mention how slow and clumsy it was, but

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: scientists now believe the bird's strong knee joints would have made it capable of

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: movement which was not slow, but actually quite fast.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: In fact, one 17th century sailor wrote that he found the birds hard to catch.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: It's true that the dodo's small wings wouldn't have allowed it to leave the ground, but

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: the scientists suggest that these were probably employed for balance while going over

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: uneven ground. Another group of scientists carried out analysis of the dodo's skull.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: They found that the reports of the lack of intelligence of the dodo were not borne out by

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: their research, which suggested the bird's brain was not small, but average in size.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: In fact, in relation to its body size, it was similar to that of the pigeon, which is

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: known to be a highly intelligent bird.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: The researchers also found that the structure of the bird's skull suggested that one

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: sense which was particularly well-developed was that of smell.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: So the dodo may also have been particularly good at locating ripe fruit and other food in

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: the island's thick vegetation.
